bullets.text: Machine Learning (ML) is a subfield of Artificial Intelligence (AI).
ML systems learn patterns from data rather than being explicitly programmed.
Models improve over time with more data without needing reprogramming.
It's about teaching computers to learn from experience, like humans.
ML is ubiquitous, powering recommendations, spam filters, and virtual assistants.
Growth is due to access to vast amounts of data.
Increased computational power (GPUs) enables efficient data processing.
Development of sophisticated algorithms extracts better insights.
Most common type, trains models using labeled data (input + correct output).
Model learns relationships to predict outputs for new inputs.
Regression predicts continuous values (e.g., house price, temperature).
Classification predicts discrete labels or categories (e.g., spam detection).
Uses unlabeled data, with no explicit answers provided.
Goal is to discover patterns, relationships, or structures independently.
Clustering groups similar data points (e.g., customer segmentation).
Dimensionality reduction simplifies data with many features.
An agent learns by interacting with an environment.
Receives feedback as rewards or penalties for its decisions.
Goal is to learn a policy that maximizes total reward over time.
Examples include training robots to walk or AI playing games like chess.
Data quality is crucial; noisy, biased, or incomplete data harms performance.
Overfitting occurs when a model learns training data too well but fails to generalize.
Ethical concerns arise from biased data leading to biased models.
Understanding data context and real-world impact is essential.
